findings.summary: Lean states the comparison for any smooth reference solution with fixed compact support on [0,T]. The force drops out as equal residuals, so the specific u of Prop 10.1 and f of Lemma 10.3 are not needed. This is a strictly more general statement.

candidate_unique_on_Icc takes the whole CandidateProperties bundle, including speed_unbounded and energy_bounded, which Lemma 10.5 does not use. Applying that form to the paper's u would therefore also need (10.21) and Lemma 10.4. classical_uniqueness_on_Icc has no such dependency, and the main theorem uses it.

v ∈ L^∞([0,T];L²) appears as UniformFiniteEnergy: a bound on ½∫|v(t)|² at every t∈[0,T], not almost every t. For continuous v the two agree by Fatou's lemma, because every time is a limit of good times.

The proof route differs from the paper's. The pressure-flux bound (10.19) is checked in a different envelope, (B^{1/2}+1)(A/R+R^{-2})+R^{-7/4}B^{3/4}, using L^{6/5}–L^6 duality and a heat-kernel R_iR_j representation rather than L^{3/2} and Calderón–Zygmund. So the paper's argument as written is not what was checked, but the result is unaffected.
